Story cutoffs computed from 15:00 SGT on 8 Aug: top_stories/singapore = items published after 2026-08-07T15:00+08:00; cybersecurity = after 2026-08-05T15:00+08:00; wars/outbreaks = last 14 days. cdc.gov and moe.gov.sg both refused direct fetches this run (HTTP 403/404), so CDC figures come from CDC-attributed reporting and the MOE teacher-AI plan is attributed to The Straits Times' report. ECDC's threat-report RSS still has nothing newer than 20 July, but its live Ebola outbreak page was readable and is used for the DR Congo national figures.

top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Russian missiles killed three people, one of them a child, in the Kyiv region overnight — hours after a US official revealed Kyiv had quietly agreed to stop hitting some non-Russian tankers and the Black Sea terminal that exports Kazakh crude. The Middle East realigned fast, with Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signing a mutual-defence pact that treats an armed attack on one as an attack on all three. Washington now expects an Iran–Oman deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days, though Yemen is going the other way as Houthi missiles hit displacement camps in Marib. At home the White House moved again to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook, days after a surprise fall in US payrolls knocked the dollar down and pushed shares up. Watch the Hormuz talks — a deal there would move oil and shipping costs faster than anything else on today's list.

stories.headline: Russian missile strikes kill three, including a child, in the Kyiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian regional officials say three people were killed, among them a child, in overnight Russian missile attacks on settlements near Kyiv. Casualty figures come from Ukrainian authorities and have not been independently verified; Moscow says it strikes only military targets.

stories.headline: US says Ukraine has agreed not to target some tankers and a Black Sea oil terminal
stories.summary: A US official says Kyiv has committed to sparing non-Russian tankers and the Caspian Pipeline Consortium infrastructure near Novorossiysk that carries Kazakh crude, after strikes last month halted loadings. The exemption applies to vessels not sanctioned by Ukraine, not carrying Russian cargo and not Russian-owned; Kyiv has set up contact points for commercial shippers. Reported by Bloomberg and The Straits Times.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan sign a mutual-defence pact
stories.summary: The three Sunni-majority powers signed an agreement treating an armed attack on any one of them as an attack on all, the most significant security realignment in the region since the US–Israel strikes on Iran in February. The signatories frame it as deterrence; regional analysts note it also draws nuclear-armed Pakistan into Gulf security guarantees.
stories.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

stories.headline: US official expects an Iran–Oman deal on the Strait of Hormuz 'soon'
stories.summary: A US official says an agreement between Iran and Oman to restore shipping through the strait is expected shortly, with any temporary routes carrying 'no approved' cargo restrictions still under negotiation. Iran has separately said it wants US and Israeli-linked vessels barred as part of any accord — a condition Washington has not accepted. Both sides' positions are claims pending a signed text.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Marib again as the UN warns Yemen risks being pulled into a wider war
stories.summary: Houthi missiles and drones hit displacement camps and residential areas in Marib, according to Yemeni government officials, days after attacks that Yemeni forces said killed at least 30 of their personnel. The UN envoy warned the escalation risks drawing Yemen fully into the regional conflict. Casualty counts come from one party to the war and are not independently verified.

stories.headline: US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July, sending the dollar down and shares up
stories.summary: US payrolls fell last month against forecasts of a solid gain, in a labour-market miss that markets read as removing pressure for further rate rises. The dollar dropped, equities climbed and the yen surged far enough that traders began watching for Japanese intervention.

stories.headline: Trump renews his effort to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook
stories.summary: The White House sent Cook a letter saying the president is considering removing her over unproven mortgage-fraud allegations, roughly a month after the Supreme Court blocked an earlier attempt and ruled she was entitled to notice and a chance to respond. She has been given until 26 August to reply. Cook denies the allegations and her lawyers say there is no valid cause; no president has removed a Fed governor since the central bank was founded in 1913.
stories.source: The Straits Times, The Washington Post, NPR, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: US appeals court halts Trump's US$400 million White House ballroom
stories.summary: An appeals court ordered construction stopped on the privately funded ballroom project, setting up a likely Supreme Court appeal. It is the latest in a run of adverse rulings for the administration over executive authority and federal property.
stories.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

stories.headline: US Senate passes a sweeping Russia sanctions bill
stories.summary: The Senate approved legislation targeting Russian officials, banks and energy revenues, with a large bipartisan majority. The bill still needs to clear the House before it can reach the president's desk.

stories.headline: Trump touts about US$3 billion in critical-minerals projects to counter China
stories.summary: At a State Department roundtable with mining executives, the president announced financing for domestic minerals projects, including a US$1.4 billion conditional loan to battery-materials firm Sila Nanotechnologies, US$400 million to scandium miner Sunrise Energy Metals and US$150 million to magnet developer Niron Magnetics. Bloomberg, Reuters and the White House put the headline figure at about US$3 billion; The Straits Times reported US$3.8 billion.
stories.source: Bloomberg, The Straits Times, The White House

stories.headline: Pentagon sets funding and dates for the secret Golden Dome space programme
stories.summary: The Pentagon has fixed a schedule for its space-based missile-defence shield, aiming for first tests by year-end and flight demonstrations of the unproven interceptor technology in 2027. Reported by Bloomberg and carried by The Straits Times.

stories.headline: EU tells Meta and TikTok to step up monitoring and fact-checking after Ceuta
stories.summary: EU tech commissioner Henna Virkkunen said after talks with both platforms that 'monitoring must increase' and cooperation with fact-checkers must be strengthened, following the social-media rumour that the Ceuta border had opened and the mass crossing that followed. The Commission said it would follow up on Monday.

stories.headline: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as the Ceuta migration row escalates
stories.summary: Madrid introduced controls on travellers arriving from Italy after Rome declined to lift its own curbs, an unusual breakdown of free movement between two EU founding-era partners. Italy has publicly defied the Spanish demand; the Commission has urged both sides to de-escalate.
stories.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

stories.headline: Thai PM promises stricter gun laws after a school shooting that killed eight
stories.summary: The prime minister said gun controls would be tightened after a 14-year-old killed his grandparents and then opened fire at a school in Nonthaburi, near Bangkok. CNA has since published a reconstruction of how the attacker obtained the weapon and moved between the two scenes.

stories.headline: Floods in India's north-east kill nearly 100
stories.summary: Assam and neighbouring states are counting the dead after days of flooding, with the toll approaching 100 according to state disaster authorities. Rescue and relief operations are continuing and the figure is expected to be revised.

stories.headline: Germany treats an explosive drone found at an airport as a possible hybrid attack; Russia calls it fabricated
stories.summary: Germany's federal prosecutor has taken over the investigation into an explosives-laden drone found near a Ukrainian aircraft, and a lawmaker said a bus driver kicked the device out of the air. Berlin has held a security meeting and officials have described it as 'a hybrid attack'; Russia's foreign ministry dismissed the incident as a 'fabricated provocation'. No attribution has been established.

stories.headline: Zelensky makes a landmark first visit to Serbia
stories.summary: The Ukrainian president visited Belgrade for the first time since the full-scale invasion began, a notable stop given Serbia's long-standing ties to Moscow and its dependence on Russian gas.

stories.headline: Meta fined US$567 million in the largest child-safety ruling against a social media company
stories.summary: A US state court ordered Meta to pay into a teen mental-health fund, the largest penalty of its kind against a social media platform to date. Meta is expected to appeal.

stories.headline: Spanish police arrest 78 in what they call one of the Mediterranean's largest smuggling busts
stories.summary: Officers dismantled a network Spain describes as among the largest human-smuggling operations in the Mediterranean, arresting 78 people. The 'largest' framing is the Spanish authorities' own characterisation.

stories.headline: US plans US$1 billion in security assistance for Colombia's new government
stories.summary: Washington says it intends to provide about US$1 billion in security aid to the incoming Colombian administration, a sharp reset after a period of strained relations over counter-narcotics policy.

stories.headline: Trump administration to pay a German firm US$1.2 billion to halt US offshore wind projects
stories.summary: The administration agreed to pay the developer to abandon planned US offshore wind projects, an unusual use of public money to stop rather than start energy construction. Critics have questioned the legal basis; the administration frames it as a cost saving.

stories.headline: China's new PLA leadership points to an unfinished military rebuild under Xi
stories.summary: CNA analyses the latest round of People's Liberation Army promotions and reshuffles, arguing the pattern of anti-corruption removals and replacements shows Xi Jinping's restructuring of the armed forces is still in progress rather than complete.

stories.headline: Nurul Izzah takes leave from her PKR deputy president post
stories.summary: Anwar Ibrahim's daughter has stepped back from her role as deputy president of Malaysia's PKR, raising questions about succession and factional balance inside the governing party.

stories.headline: Indonesia battles a Mount Bromo wildfire as El Niño takes hold
stories.summary: Firefighters are working to contain a blaze on the slopes of Mount Bromo in East Java, one of several fires as drier El Niño conditions set in across the archipelago.

stories.headline: Brazil's Amazon deforestation rate approaches a historic low
stories.summary: Official monitoring data show clearing in the Brazilian Amazon nearing the lowest level on record, continuing a multi-year decline. Researchers caution that fire and degradation figures tell a less positive story than the clear-cut rate alone.

stories.headline: Mexico and Peru restore diplomatic relations after an asylum row
stories.summary: The two countries agreed to resume full diplomatic ties, ending a rupture that followed Mexico's grant of asylum to a Peruvian politician.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Every primary, secondary and junior college teacher will have to complete compulsory AI modules under a new Ministry of Education plan reported by The Straits Times — the clearest sign yet that AI training is becoming part of the job rather than an optional add-on. The courts did the rest of the heavy lifting, with two men charged over allegedly arranging Lim Tean's exit to Johor and a driver charged over the death of a petrol station attendant while allegedly under the influence of drugs. Elsewhere the state was busy with energy and land: conditional approval to import solar power from Malaysia, and a public consultation on protecting genetic information. The buzz is nostalgic this National Day weekend, led by Tiger Beer's final Singapore brew and a hunt for the HDB blocks that appeared in NDP 2000's 'Shine On Me' video. Expect the Lim Tean case and the Fun Coffee arrests to keep moving next week.

stories.headline: All primary, secondary and JC teachers to complete compulsory AI modules under a new MOE plan
stories.summary: The Straits Times reports that the Ministry of Education will require every teacher in primary schools, secondary schools and junior colleges to complete mandatory artificial-intelligence modules, extending AI training from an optional professional-development track to a requirement. MOE's own newsroom pages were unreachable this run, so the details rest on ST's report.

stories.headline: Two men charged over allegedly arranging Lim Tean's illegal exit to Johor
stories.summary: Two men were charged over allegedly conspiring to help lawyer Lim Tean leave Singapore without clearing immigration, days after he failed to surrender at the State Courts to begin his jail term. Lim was arrested in Johor Bahru; Chinese-language daily Shin Min reported he had no passport with him and did not open the door to officers for about two hours.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times, Mothership/Shin Min

stories.headline: Driver charged over the death of a petrol station attendant was allegedly on drugs
stories.summary: The man charged with causing the death of a pump attendant was allegedly under the influence of drugs and driving a deregistered car without a licence, according to charge sheets. The case adds to a run of drug-driving prosecutions this week.

stories.headline: Investigation names scam kingpin Chen Zhi's top associates and their Singapore assets
stories.summary: A six-month investigation by The Straits Times with the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project identifies senior figures in the Prince Group syndicate and the property, company shareholdings and family-office structures they held in Singapore. Singapore police have previously announced asset seizures linked to the network.

stories.headline: Woman arrested after the collapse of the alleged 'Fun Coffee' Ponzi scheme
stories.summary: Police arrested a woman in Singapore following the collapse of an alleged Ponzi scheme marketed as 'Fun Coffee'. Victims in Singapore, Hong Kong and Macau are reported to have lost millions; the total loss figure has not been confirmed by police.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist, 58, injured in the Aug 4 SLE accident dies
stories.summary: A 58-year-old motorcyclist who was hurt in an accident on the Seletar Expressway on 4 August has died of his injuries.

stories.headline: Elderly residents on fire risk after a spate of fatal blazes
stories.summary: The Straits Times speaks to older residents about safety in their flats after a series of fatal fires, finding a mix of fatalism and practical worry about escape routes, clutter and mobility.

stories.headline: Three arrested over a scheme that compromised work permit holders' Singpass accounts
stories.summary: Police arrested three people over an operation that allegedly took control of Singpass accounts belonging to work permit holders. Compromised Singpass credentials have repeatedly been used as an entry point for scam and money-laundering operations.

stories.headline: Singapore grants conditional approval to import solar power from Malaysia
stories.summary: The Energy Market Authority gave conditional approvals for solar electricity imports from Malaysia, part of Singapore's plan to draw a share of its power from low-carbon regional sources. Conditional approval is an early step; commercial and grid agreements still have to follow.

stories.headline: Grace Fu says her ministry has no mandate over Maju Forest land-use planning
stories.summary: Responding to calls to protect Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, Minister Grace Fu said land-use planning falls outside the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment's remit. The clarification comes as public pressure over both sites continues.

stories.headline: NParks begins sterilising long-tailed macaques at Maju Forest
stories.summary: NParks has started a sterilisation programme for long-tailed macaques at Maju Forest to manage the population, saying it is a less drastic alternative to culling where human-macaque conflict is rising.

stories.headline: Renaming MTI the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry is more than a rebrand, experts say
stories.summary: Analysts tell The Straits Times the addition of 'Energy' to the ministry's name signals that energy security and the power transition are being folded into Singapore's core economic strategy rather than treated as an environmental side-file.

stories.headline: 8kg of cocaine seized from a foreign-registered vessel in Singapore waters
stories.summary: Authorities recovered about 8kg of cocaine from a foreign-registered commercial ship in Singapore waters, in one of the larger maritime seizures reported this year.

stories.headline: Co-living scheme for young Singaporeans is five times oversubscribed
stories.summary: More than 500 young Singaporeans applied for a limited batch of co-living rooms, leaving the scheme about five times oversubscribed — another signal of demand for interim housing among singles who cannot yet buy a flat.

stories.headline: Public consultation opens on proposed laws to protect genetic information
stories.summary: The government has opened a public consultation on legislation governing how genetic information can be collected, used and shared, including limits on use by insurers and employers.

stories.headline: Ex-Sakae Holdings director jailed more than 10 years for misappropriating S$15.8 million
stories.summary: A former director of Sakae Holdings was sentenced to over 10 years' jail for misappropriating S$15.8 million and lying in the High Court.

stories.headline: Jail for a training officer who shoved a woman with an intellectual disability
stories.summary: A former training officer was jailed for pushing a woman with an intellectual disability in his care, causing knee fractures.

stories.headline: Man jailed for faking glove and mask supplies during Covid-19, cheating 11 victims of S$3.79 million
stories.summary: A man was jailed for pretending to supply gloves and face masks during the pandemic, cheating 11 victims of a combined S$3.79 million.

stories.headline: Man jailed over 179 upskirt videos and molesting a woman at an MRT station
stories.summary: A man was sentenced to jail after taking 179 upskirt videos over three years and molesting a woman at an MRT station.

stories.headline: Singapore recruits its first nurses from Bhutan
stories.summary: Singapore has begun hiring nurses from Bhutan as it widens the countries it draws healthcare staff from, part of a longer push to diversify a workforce heavily reliant on a few source countries.

stories.headline: Man dies after a traffic accident in Hougang
stories.summary: A man died following a traffic accident in Hougang; police are investigating.

stories.headline: CNB investigating the online sale of a Trader Joe's seasoning containing poppy seeds
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau is looking into online sales of a Trader Joe's seasoning product that contains poppy seeds, which are a controlled item in Singapore.

stories.headline: Dead fish at Sungei Buloh were likely trapped and killed by the hot weather, NParks says
stories.summary: NParks said fish found dead at Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve were most likely trapped in shallow pools and died as recent hot weather raised water temperatures and cut oxygen levels, rather than from pollution.

stories.headline: Director behind firms in the unpaid workers case files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: The director of the companies at the centre of an unpaid-wages case has filed for bankruptcy, complicating recovery for the affected workers.

stories.headline: Man given a police award for helping arrest a suspected thief on a flight to Singapore
stories.summary: Police presented an award to a passenger who helped detain a suspected thief on board a flight into Singapore.

stories.headline: Man, 40, charged with abusing his daughter and ordering his son to strip and go downstairs
stories.summary: A 40-year-old man was charged over physically abusing his eight-year-old daughter and telling his 10-year-old son to strip naked and go to the ground floor of their HDB block.

stories.headline: Malaysian man, 43, found dead in a drain; family disputes the police finding
stories.summary: The family of a 43-year-old Malaysian man found dead and unclothed in a drain is disputing the police conclusion that he fell in while drunk, and has asked for further investigation. The family's account and the police finding are both single-source claims at this stage.

stories.headline: Singapore reach the ASEAN championship semi-finals after drawing with Indonesia
stories.summary: The Lions drew with Indonesia to qualify for the ASEAN football championship semi-finals. Coach Gavin Lee said afterwards that 'nobody gave us a chance in this group'.

stories.headline: Tiger Beer employees prepare for the last brew made in Singapore
stories.summary: The Straits Times goes inside the brewery as staff work through the final Singapore-brewed batch of Tiger Beer, closing a chapter that started in 1932.

stories.headline: Singaporeans think they have found the HDB blocks from NDP 2000's 'Shine On Me' video
stories.summary: A crowd-sourced hunt for the flats that appear in the National Day Parade 2000 music video has converged on blocks in Serangoon North, with residents and old photos being used to check the match.

stories.headline: Two National Day films spark an 'AI slop' debate
stories.summary: Two Singapore films released for National Day have drawn criticism over their use of generative AI, with viewers split between calling the work 'AI slop' and defending it as a legitimate low-budget tool.

stories.headline: AI short film puts 'Lionara' in a zombie outbreak with the NDP as backdrop
stories.summary: A separate AI-generated short film imagines a zombie attack during the National Day Parade, featuring the mascot 'Lionara'. It has circulated widely alongside the debate over AI in this year's National Day films.

stories.headline: Singapore woman dies at 109, having gone from hiding in a coffin in WW2 to running a farm
stories.summary: A Singaporean woman who died at 109 is remembered for surviving the Japanese Occupation — including hiding in a coffin — and later building a successful farm.

stories.headline: Thai food stall offers a free buffet to diners hit by the Yishun coffee shop fire
stories.summary: A Thai food stall is offering free buffet meals to customers and neighbours affected by a fire at a Yishun coffee shop.

stories.headline: Man, 36, fined S$3,000 after refusing to pay for porridge and harassing police at Orchard Plaza
stories.summary: A drunk 36-year-old man was fined S$3,000 after refusing to pay for porridge at Orchard Plaza and then harassing the police officers who responded.

stories.headline: Tourist apologises for paying a Vietnamese taxi driver with 'thank you' instead of cash
stories.summary: A tourist has publicly apologised after leaving a Vietnamese taxi driver unpaid, in a clip that circulated widely among Singapore readers this week.

stories.headline: A start-up founded by Singapore poly graduates makes it into Y Combinator
stories.summary: The Straits Times profiles a Singapore start-up founded by polytechnic graduates that has been accepted into the Silicon Valley accelerator Y Combinator.

stories.headline: A giant map of Singapore built from 28,000 bottle caps
stories.summary: A large map of Singapore assembled from about 28,000 recycled bottle caps has gone on display, part of a recycling-awareness project.

stories.headline: Nerf bullets, a slipper and underwear among the litter jamming reverse vending machines
stories.summary: Operators say machines meant to collect recyclable bottles and cans are being fed everything from a Nerf gun bullet to underwear, causing jams and contamination.

stories.headline: Where to catch the NDP 2026 fireworks
stories.summary: The Straits Times lists six vantage points for watching the National Day Parade fireworks, with tips for photographing them.

stories.headline: She quit school twice; now her horror art studio's neon art jams book out most weekends
stories.summary: CNA profiles the founder of a horror-themed art studio in Singapore that nearly closed before its neon art-jam sessions began selling out at weekends.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Russia's war on Ukraine is now partly a fight over shipping lanes: under US pressure, Kyiv has agreed to stop striking some non-Russian tankers and the Black Sea terminal that exports Kazakh crude, narrowing a target set it had been widening all year. That restraint has not been reciprocated on land, where Russian missiles killed three people including a child in the Kyiv region overnight. The Gulf is moving the other way — toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — but the new Saudi–Türkiye–Pakistan pact changes the region's arithmetic more than the deal does, since a strike on any one of them now pulls in two more. Lebanon, meanwhile, is quietly assembling the machinery to verify Hezbollah's disarmament. The thing to watch is Yemen, where intensifying Houthi strikes on Marib could undo the Hormuz progress before it is signed.

theatres.name: Russia–Ukraine War
theatres.status: Long-range strikes continuing on both sides, but Washington has begun shaping Ukraine's target list at sea while Europe treats sabotage on its own soil as part of the war

timeline.event: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The war is now in its fifth year.
After a deadly strike on Kyiv, Ukraine warns that its shortage of air-defence interceptors is costing lives. Patriot stocks are depleted worldwide.
Ukraine hits two oil refineries deep inside Russian territory; BBC News reports from Odesa on a widening pattern of Russian strikes in the Black Sea region.
The US Senate passes a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Russian officials, banks and energy revenues. It still requires House approval.

Germany holds a security meeting over an explosives-laden drone found near a Ukrainian aircraft at an airport, with the federal prosecutor taking over the case; officials call it 'a hybrid attack'. Russia's foreign ministry dismisses the incident as a 'fabricated provocation'.
Zelensky makes his first visit to Serbia, a long-standing Russian ally and gas customer.

A US official says Ukraine has agreed not to target some non-Russian tankers or the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's Black Sea terminal near Novorossiysk, after strikes last month halted Kazakh crude loadings.
Russian missile attacks on the Kyiv region kill three people, including a child, according to Ukrainian regional officials.

theatres.name: US/Israel–Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Closest yet to a shipping deal — US officials expect an Iran–Oman agreement within days — but a new Sunni defence bloc has formed and Yemen is deteriorating

timeline.event: The United States and Israel attack Iran. Tehran responds by largely closing the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of seaborne oil passes.
President Trump says he has cancelled planned strikes on Iran, conditional on a deal being made 'rapidly'.
Iran says a deal with Oman on reopening the strait is in its final stages.
Israel dismisses senior intelligence officials, with reporting attributing the shake-up to an expanding Iranian spy network.
Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan sign a mutual-defence pact treating an armed attack on one as an attack on all three.
timeline.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

timeline.event: A US official says an Iran–Oman deal on the strait is expected soon. Iran has said it wants US and Israeli-linked vessels barred as part of any accord, a condition Washington has not accepted.

Houthi missiles and drones hit displacement camps and residential areas in Marib, Yemeni government officials say, days after attacks they said killed at least 30 government troops. The UN envoy warns Yemen risks being drawn into the wider conflict.
Iraq's prime minister and Saudi Arabia's intelligence chief discuss regional security as Iran-aligned Iraqi militias hold off on responding to the pact.

theatres.name: Israel–Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Verification machinery for Hezbollah's disarmament is being assembled, while strikes continue in Gaza and southern Lebanon

timeline.event: BBC News sets out the Gaza peace-deal roadmap after Hamas signals acceptance of a disarmament framework.
At least 13 people are killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza after Hamas agreed the disarmament deal, Palestinian officials say.
Israel strikes southern Lebanon after two of its soldiers are killed by an explosion, testing the ceasefire.
Rights groups say an Israeli attack that killed a Lebanese journalist appears to be a war crime. Israel has not accepted that characterisation.
Israel charges a settler over the killing of a Palestinian who was involved in an Oscar-winning film about the West Bank.
Lebanon and Israel agree a short-list of countries that could send troops to verify Hezbollah's disarmament.
US senators introduce a Lebanon aid bill that ties assistance to measures countering Hezbollah.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic keeps outrunning the official count: the health ministry's own tally is now several hundred cases ahead of WHO's last ratified figure, and this is already the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country. Uganda, at least, was declared Ebola-free at the end of July after 20 cases. In the US the picture is chronic rather than acute — measles at a 35-year high with no deaths so far, and a Salmonella outbreak traced to jalapeños from a single Mexican growing region. If you are travelling to eastern DR Congo, expect exit screening and treat the WHO number as a floor rather than a ceiling.

outbreaks.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DR Congo, Uganda, France
outbreaks.status: Largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in DR Congo and still expanding; Uganda declared free of the disease on 28 July
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cases only, as of 30 July 2026, from Disease Outbreak News 614 published 1 August: DR Congo 3,605 confirmed cases with 1,587 deaths (case-fatality ratio 44%), Uganda 20 with 2 deaths, France 1. Two DR Congo patients were also treated in Germany. The outbreak was active in 33 of 49 affected health zones, with Ituri province accounting for 88% of cases. Newer than the DON and not yet WHO-ratified: ECDC reports that on 6 August DR Congo published a situation update giving 4,053 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths as of 5 August. Uganda was declared Ebola-free on 28 July 2026.

outbreaks.name: Measles — United States
outbreaks.status: Highest US annual case count since 1991; no deaths recorded so far this year
outbreaks.scope_note: US CDC surveillance data as of 6 August 2026: 2,465 confirmed cases in 2026, ahead of 2025's full-year total of 2,289 and the highest since 1991. CDC reports 93% of infected people were unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status, and no measles deaths in the US in 2026. cdc.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch attempts this run, so these figures come from CDC-attributed reporting rather than a page read directly.

outbreaks.name: Salmonella Javiana — United States (jalapeños)
outbreaks.status: Traced to jalapeños grown in Sinaloa, Mexico; recalled product pulled by restaurant chains
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC/FDA outbreak tally announced 5 August 2026: 345 illnesses across 27 states, 36 hospitalisations and no deaths, with illness onsets from 19 June to 20 July 2026. Minnesota and Colorado account for roughly two-thirds of cases. Of 191 people interviewed, 177 (93%) had eaten at a Mexican-style restaurant, including Chipotle and QDOBA. Traceback points to fresh jalapeños grown in Sinaloa, Mexico and distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors. CDC notes the true case count is likely higher.

outbreaks.name: Andes hantavirus — MV Hondius cruise cluster
outbreaks.status: Ship cluster closed out; WHO figures are now more than five weeks old
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON611 figures as of 2 July 2026: 13 cases (12 confirmed, one probable) including three deaths, all among people who travelled on the M/V Hondius; case-fatality ratio 23%. WHO has issued no update since, so these numbers are stale and the entry is retained only for continuity. 'Countries' is not a single figure — cases were reported across several countries plus Tristan da Cunha.

stories.headline: DR Congo passes 4,000 confirmed Ebola cases as Uganda is declared free of the disease
stories.summary: ECDC's outbreak page records that DR Congo's 6 August situation update reported 4,053 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths as of 5 August — several hundred more than WHO's last formally ratified count from 30 July. Uganda was declared Ebola-free on 28 July after 20 confirmed cases and two deaths. ECDC's next epidemiological update is due on 10 August.
stories.source: ECDC, DR Congo Ministry of Health

stories.headline: Seven passengers on a boat intercepted near Kinshasa test negative for Ebola
stories.summary: Seven people taken off a river boat intercepted near Kinshasa tested negative for Ebola, easing fears that the outbreak had reached the capital via the Congo River. Screening of river traffic is continuing.

stories.headline: US measles cases reach a 35-year high at 2,465 confirmed
stories.summary: CDC data as of 6 August put 2026 measles cases at 2,465, above 2025's full-year total of 2,289 and the highest annual count since 1991. No deaths have been recorded in 2026; CDC reports 93% of those infected were unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status.

stories.headline: Jalapeño-linked Salmonella outbreak has sickened 345 people across 27 states
stories.summary: CDC and FDA said on 5 August that 345 people in 27 states have been infected with Salmonella Javiana traced to fresh jalapeños grown in Sinaloa, Mexico. Thirty-six people have been hospitalised and there have been no deaths; illness onsets run from 19 June to 20 July. Two isolates showed antibiotic resistance.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Metabase first: an unauthenticated SQL-injection flaw with no CVE and a CVSS of 10.0 was exploited as a zero-day to steal customer data from laptop maker Framework, and self-hosted instances stay exposed until they are updated. After that it is a heavy vendor cycle — Cisco shipped fixes for twelve SD-WAN and IOS XE bugs including three scoring 9.9, and a CVSS 10.0 cross-tenant flaw in Terraform's MCP server headlines a batch alongside Veeam and Django. CISA added an actively exploited JetBrains TeamCity RCE to its known-exploited catalog, which makes that one a deadline rather than a suggestion. The week's other theme is AI tooling becoming attack surface: a malicious GitHub issue could reach CI secrets through Claude Code and Gemini CLI, and agent frameworks from AWS, Google and Vercel could be made to run tools without the model ever being invoked. Assume your developer supply chain is the target this cycle.

stories.headline: Metabase SQL-injection zero-day exploited to steal customer data
stories.summary: Metabase's advisory rates an unauthenticated SQL-injection flaw in its password-reset endpoint at CVSS 10.0 and confirms active exploitation; no CVE has been assigned. Versions 58 through 63 of both Metabase Cloud and self-hosted deployments are affected, with fixes in x.58.24, x.59.21, x.60.17, x.61.11, x.62.9 and x.63.5. Laptop maker Framework says attackers used it to take names, email addresses, phone numbers and physical addresses for its entire customer base.

stories.headline: Unlimited Technology Systems breach affects 3.8 million people
stories.summary: The physical-security and technology services firm is notifying about 3.8 million people that their data was exposed in a breach. The company has not detailed the initial access vector.

stories.headline: Nearly 800 malicious npm packages deliver a cross-platform RAT and infostealer
stories.summary: Researchers catalogued close to 800 malicious npm packages that install a remote-access trojan and credential stealer on Windows, macOS and Linux. The campaign is an escalation of a smaller wave that targeted Alibaba tooling users earlier in the week.

stories.headline: ClickFix lures deliver a macOS stealer that drains crypto wallets
stories.summary: Fake 'fix this error' prompts are pushing a macOS infostealer built to empty cryptocurrency wallets. Researchers also counted more than 250 ClickFix domains using browser fingerprinting to show the macOS lure only to Mac visitors, keeping it away from analysts.

stories.headline: UNC6671 phones staff on personal mobiles to talk them out of SaaS data
stories.summary: The extortion group, linked to the BlackFile operation, is calling employees on their personal phones — outside corporate monitoring — to social-engineer access to SaaS platforms. Hedge funds are among the reported victims.

stories.headline: North Carolina Ports confirms a cyberattack disrupting operations
stories.summary: The port authority confirmed a cyberattack that has disrupted operations. No group has claimed responsibility and the authority has not said whether ransomware was involved.

stories.headline: WordPress patches a pre-auth login XSS that can be chained to PHP execution
stories.summary: A pre-authentication reflected cross-site scripting flaw on the WordPress login screen can, via a crafted link, be chained to PHP code execution. NVD scores it 8.9. Patch immediately — WordPress Core flaws have twice landed in CISA's known-exploited catalog in the last three weeks.

stories.headline: An 18-year-old Linux SCTP flaw gives local root and container escape
stories.summary: A bug in the kernel's SCTP handling, present for roughly 18 years, lets a local user gain root and escape containers. NVD lists the record without a CVSS score; the kernel fix stops the ASCONF path from freeing its own transport.

stories.headline: NatJack attacks hijack TCP sessions and spoof DNS by manipulating NAT tables
stories.summary: An origin-validation error in Windows Network Address Translation lets an unauthorised attacker spoof traffic, enabling TCP session hijacking and DNS spoofing from off-path. NVD scores it 8.3.

stories.headline: AI-assisted research finds new HTTP desync techniques and an Apache Traffic Server zero-day
stories.summary: James Kettle's HTTP Terminator generated about 30,000 candidate attack vectors from 138 HTTP and SMTP RFCs and proved several new request-smuggling techniques, one of which exposed more than 200 test-set websites. A malformed request also surfaced a desynchronisation zero-day in Apache Traffic Server, since patched and tracked as CVE-2026-63078. The CVE is not yet published in NVD.

stories.headline: Claude Code and Gemini CLI flaws let a GitHub issue reach CI workflow secrets
stories.summary: Flaws in both AI coding assistants allowed a malicious GitHub issue to reach secrets held by CI workflows. The Gemini CLI side is tracked as CVE-2026-12537, an OS command-injection issue in the container launcher scored 10.0 by NVD and fixed in 0.39.1. Anthropic and Google have both shipped fixes; audit any repository where either tool runs in automation.

stories.headline: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
stories.summary: Swiss federal authorities say about 200 accounts were compromised in a breach of a government SharePoint deployment. Two SharePoint deserialisation flaws were added to CISA's known-exploited catalog last month.

stories.headline: TONTOU interrupt-injection attack bypasses Spectre v2 defences on Intel and AMD
stories.summary: Researchers showed that injecting interrupts at precise moments defeats existing Spectre v2 mitigations on both Intel and AMD processors, and demonstrated leaking Linux password hashes. Exploitation requires local code execution.

stories.headline: Zapscape KVM flaw lets privileged L1 guest code escape to the Linux host
stories.summary: A KVM bug allows privileged code inside a first-level guest to break out to the Linux host, a serious issue for multi-tenant virtualisation. NVD lists the record without a CVSS score; the fix reorders a check for invalid or obsolete roots.

stories.headline: Cisco patches 12 SD-WAN and IOS XE flaws, three of them scoring 9.9
stories.summary: Cisco released fixes for a dozen Catalyst SD-WAN and IOS XE vulnerabilities found in an internal security review, three of which carry a CVSS of 9.9. NVD confirms 9.9 for CVE-2026-20303. Cisco says it is not aware of exploitation, but network-edge devices are a standing target.

stories.headline: Over 4,400 Rockwell PLCs are exposed online, 22 in cities hit by water-system attacks
stories.summary: Scanning found more than 4,400 Rockwell programmable logic controllers reachable from the internet, including 22 in municipalities previously targeted in attacks on water systems. Exposed PLCs generally have no authentication and should not face the internet at all.

stories.headline: Weak randomness in CryptoJS is behind about US$5.7 million in wallet drains
stories.summary: A weak random-number generator in the CryptoJS library made private keys predictable in five cryptocurrency wallet apps, and researchers attribute roughly US$5.7 million in drained funds to it. Any wallet generated with the affected code path should be treated as compromised.

stories.headline: Attackers compile the khunt toolkit inside Oracle to turn SQL injection into SYSTEM access
stories.summary: Intruders are using Oracle Database's built-in Java compiler to build a post-exploitation toolkit in place, escalating a SQL-injection foothold to Windows SYSTEM without dropping a recognisable binary on disk.

stories.headline: CoreBreak: AWS, Google and Vercel agent flaws let attackers trigger tools without running the model
stories.summary: Flaws in three major agent frameworks allow tool calls to be executed without the underlying model being invoked, bypassing the confirmation step that is supposed to gate dangerous actions. Google's Agent Development Kit issue, a continuation-forgery bug in tool confirmations, is tracked as CVE-2026-18236 and scored 9.3 by NVD. All three vendors have shipped patches.

stories.headline: Chinese-made Zbtlink routers ship with a backdoor opening unauthenticated root shells
stories.summary: Researchers found an undocumented service in Zbtlink router firmware that hands out a root shell without authentication. No CVE has been assigned; affected devices should be replaced or firewalled off from untrusted networks.

stories.headline: CISA adds an actively exploited JetBrains TeamCity RCE to its KEV catalog
stories.summary: Unauthenticated remote code execution via the TeamCity agent polling path is under active exploitation. CISA added CVE-2026-63077 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 5 August; NVD scores it 9.8. Fixed in TeamCity 2026.1.3 and 2025.11.7.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: Poison Claude resold discounted access while its operator read every customer prompt
stories.summary: A service marketed as cut-price access to Claude routed customer traffic through an operator-controlled proxy that logged every prompt and response. Anything typed into it — including credentials and source code — should be treated as disclosed.

stories.headline: Paperclip AI flaws let attackers run host commands via malicious agent imports
stories.summary: Importing an untrusted agent definition into Paperclip AI could execute arbitrary commands on the host machine, another instance of agent configuration being treated as data when it is really code.

stories.headline: Veeam, Terraform MCP and Django patch critical flaws, led by a CVSS 10.0 cross-tenant bug
stories.summary: The headline issue is cross-tenant credential reuse in terraform-mcp-server's stateless streamable-HTTP transport before version 1.1.0, scored 10.0 by NVD — one tenant's request can end up using another tenant's credentials. Veeam and Django shipped critical fixes in the same window.

stories.headline: OVSwrap Linux kernel flaw lets local users gain root via Open vSwitch
stories.summary: A flaw in the kernel's Open vSwitch datapath gives local users root, which matters most on virtualisation and container hosts where Open vSwitch is standard.

stories.headline: Critical Gitea flaw let unauthenticated attackers read server files via Org-mode markup
stories.summary: Gitea's Org-mode renderer could be induced to include arbitrary files from the server, exposing configuration and secrets to unauthenticated visitors. The CVE is not yet published in NVD; update to the fixed release.

stories.headline: CISA flags Langflow, Apache Tomcat and N-able N-central flaws as actively exploited
stories.summary: CISA added three vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog on 3–4 August: IBM Langflow code injection (CVE-2026-9198, NVD 9.8), Apache Tomcat missing encryption of sensitive data (CVE-2026-34486, NVD 7.5) and two N-able N-central authentication bypasses (CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577) added after customer compromises. Federal agencies have binding remediation deadlines; everyone else should treat these as patch-now.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD
